titlePl: Matura PR: Podróże — 180 haseł do gier LingoSpark
titleEn: Matura Extended: Travel — 180 terms for LingoSpark games
blurbPl: Dział Podróżowanie i turystyka na maturę rozszerzoną: transport, noclegi, zwiedzanie, problemy w podróży. Fiszki ENG–PL.
blurbEn: Extended Matura travel: transport, accommodation, sightseeing and travel problems.

items.definitionEn: travelling a very long distance by air, often between continents
items.example: A long-haul flight to Australia takes over twenty hours.

items.definitionEn: a wait at an airport between two parts of a journey
items.example: We have a three-hour layover in Frankfurt.

items.definitionEn: sudden rough movement of a plane caused by air currents
items.example: The captain warned us about turbulence over the mountains.

items.definitionEn: the busy time of day when many people travel to or from work
items.example: Avoid the city centre during rush hour if you can.

items.definitionEn: a second flight that you take after changing planes
items.example: If the first plane is late, you may miss the connecting flight.

items.definitionEn: a flight hired for a tour group, not a regular scheduled service
items.example: The charter flight left at dawn from a small airport.

items.definitionEn: an airline that sells cheap tickets and charges extra for many services
items.example: A low-cost airline may charge for cabin bags and seat choice.

items.definitionEn: the door and waiting area where you enter the plane
items.example: The boarding gate closes twenty minutes before departure.

items.definitionEn: bags you take into the cabin rather than putting in the hold
items.example: Cabin baggage must fit in the overhead locker.

items.definitionEn: luggage heavier or larger than the airline's free limit, charged extra
items.example: You will pay for excess baggage if the suitcase is overweight.

items.definitionEn: the weight or number of bags you may take without extra fees
items.example: Check the baggage allowance before you pack winter boots.

items.definitionEn: the compartment above the seats for cabin bags
items.example: Put the rucksack in the overhead locker, not in the aisle.

items.definitionEn: a scheme that gives points or upgrades to regular passengers
items.example: Join the frequent-flyer programme if you travel every month.

items.definitionEn: a move to a more comfortable class of seat, sometimes free
items.example: They offered an upgrade to business class at the gate.

items.definitionEn: the cheapest, most basic seats on a plane
items.example: Most students fly economy class to save money.

items.definitionEn: a more expensive cabin with extra space and service
items.example: Business class is quieter, but the ticket costs a fortune.

items.definitionEn: an overnight flight that arrives early in the morning
items.example: The red-eye flight landed at five, and everyone looked exhausted.

items.definitionEn: failing to catch the next plane, train or bus in time
items.example: A missed connection left us in the airport until midnight.

items.definitionEn: a movable corridor that connects the terminal to the aircraft door
items.example: We boarded through the airbridge instead of a bus on the tarmac.

items.definitionEn: food, drink and help offered by cabin crew during a flight
items.example: In-flight service begins after the seat-belt sign goes off.

items.definitionEn: goods sold without tax at airports or on planes and ships
items.example: She bought perfume in duty-free after passport control.

items.definitionEn: the screen listing times and gates for leaving flights or trains
items.example: Check the departure board; the gate has changed.

items.definitionEn: the counter where you show your ticket and leave hold luggage
items.example: The check-in desk opens three hours before a long-haul departure.

items.definitionEn: a ticket stored on a phone or in an email, not printed on thick card
items.example: Show the e-ticket barcode at the gate.

items.definitionEn: at a less busy and often cheaper time to travel
items.example: Off-peak train tickets are cheaper after 9.30.

items.definitionEn: a fee for driving into a crowded city centre at busy times
items.example: London's congestion charge is payable on weekdays.

items.definitionEn: a long line of slow or stopped traffic
items.example: There is a tailback on the motorway after the accident.

items.definitionEn: repairs or building work on a road that slow traffic
items.example: Allow extra time; there are roadworks on the ring road.

items.definitionEn: a different route you must take because a road is closed
items.example: Follow the diversion signs around the closed bridge.

items.definitionEn: a road you pay to drive on
items.example: The toll road is faster but costs eight pounds.

items.definitionEn: a fast road with a strip of land between the two directions
items.example: Overtake only on a dual carriageway when it is safe.

items.definitionEn: the strip at the edge of a motorway for stopping in an emergency
items.example: Do not walk on the hard shoulder unless the car has broken down.

items.definitionEn: a road that takes traffic around a town instead of through the centre
items.example: Take the bypass if you do not need the town centre.

items.definitionEn: a short road that joins or leaves a motorway
items.example: Indicate early when you join from the slip road.

items.definitionEn: a device or app that gives driving directions using satellites
items.example: The satnav sent us down a narrow farm track by mistake.

items.definitionEn: insurance that sends help if your car stops working
items.example: Breakdown cover is wise before a long drive abroad.

items.definitionEn: a hole in a tyre that lets the air out
items.example: We had a puncture on the motorway and changed the wheel.

items.definitionEn: an extra tyre carried in a vehicle in case one fails
items.example: Check that the spare tyre has enough air before you leave.

items.definitionEn: paying to use a car for a short period
items.example: Car hire at the airport is cheaper if you book in advance.

items.definitionEn: an extra document that translates your licence for use abroad
items.example: Some countries ask for an international driving permit as well as your licence.

items.definitionEn: a journey by boat that carries people and often cars across water
items.example: The ferry crossing from Dover to Calais takes about ninety minutes.

items.definitionEn: a bus that runs back and forth between two points, such as a hotel and an airport
items.example: A free shuttle bus links the terminal and the car park.

items.definitionEn: a car park outside a city with a bus into the centre
items.example: Use park and ride to avoid paying for a city-centre space.

items.definitionEn: trains that travel much faster than ordinary services
items.example: High-speed rail from London to Paris beats most flights door to door.

items.definitionEn: a night train with beds so you travel while you sleep
items.example: The sleeper train saved us a hotel night and an early flight.

items.definitionEn: the carriage on a train where you can buy drinks and snacks
items.example: The buffet car closes after ten o'clock.

items.definitionEn: travelling by asking drivers to take you for free
items.example: Hitchhiking alone at night is not a safe idea.

items.definitionEn: several people travelling in one car to cut cost and traffic
items.example: Car sharing to the festival filled every seat.

items.definitionEn: a long-distance bus that makes few stops
items.example: The express coach from Birmingham arrives before noon.

items.definitionEn: a route for bicycles, often separated from cars
items.example: The new cycle path runs beside the river into town.

items.definitionEn: a small guesthouse that includes breakfast in the price
items.example: We booked a quiet B&B on the edge of the village.

items.definitionEn: accommodation with a kitchen so you cook your own meals
items.example: A self-catering flat is cheaper for a family of four.

items.definitionEn: accepting more reservations than there are rooms or seats
items.example: Overbooking meant two families were sent to another hotel.

items.definitionEn: a hotel deal that includes breakfast and one other meal
items.example: Half board suited us because we ate lunch in town.

items.definitionEn: a hotel deal that includes breakfast, lunch and dinner
items.example: Full board is handy if there are no restaurants nearby.

items.definitionEn: a bedroom with its own private bathroom attached
items.example: Every twin room is en suite, so you need not share a shower.

items.definitionEn: a small, stylish hotel, often with an individual design
items.example: The boutique hotel in the old town has only twelve rooms.

items.definitionEn: a flat or house rented to tourists for a short stay
items.example: The holiday let includes a kitchen and a washing machine.

items.definitionEn: a scheme where you buy the right to use a holiday property for a set week each year
items.example: They regretted the timeshare when the annual fees rose.

items.definitionEn: camping with extra comfort, such as a proper bed or a cabin
items.example: Glamping still means being outdoors, but you sleep on a mattress.

items.definitionEn: a wooden house, often in the mountains, used as holiday accommodation
items.example: The ski chalet sleeps eight and has a drying room.

items.definitionEn: a large, often detached holiday house, typically in a warm country
items.example: The villa has a private pool and a shaded terrace.

items.definitionEn: a small house in the countryside, often rented to visitors
items.example: We rented a stone cottage in the Lake District.

items.definitionEn: a home on wheels that a car can pull, used for holidays
items.example: They towed the caravan to a site near the coast.

items.definitionEn: a van fitted with beds and a small kitchen for travelling
items.example: A camper van lets you stop overnight in scenic car parks.

items.definitionEn: a hotel employee who helps guests with bookings, tickets and local advice
items.example: Ask the concierge to book a table at the harbour restaurant.

items.definitionEn: the staff or service that cleans hotel rooms
items.example: Housekeeping left fresh towels and a bottle of water.

items.definitionEn: a small fridge in a hotel room with drinks and snacks for sale
items.example: The minibar prices are higher than the shop downstairs.

items.definitionEn: permission to leave a hotel room later than the usual time
items.example: Late checkout until two o'clock costs an extra twenty pounds.

items.definitionEn: being allowed to take a room before the usual arrival time
items.example: Early check-in is useful after a night flight.

items.definitionEn: a person who has a booking but does not arrive
items.example: The hotel still charged a fee for the no-show.

items.definitionEn: a booking you cannot cancel in order to get your money back
items.example: The cheapest fare is non-refundable if your plans change.

items.definitionEn: the rules about whether you get money back if you cancel
items.example: Read the cancellation policy before you pay the deposit.

items.definitionEn: a message or document that proves your reservation is accepted
items.example: Show the booking confirmation at reception.

items.definitionEn: the price charged for a hotel room for a night
items.example: The room rate is lower if you stay midweek.

items.definitionEn: a small local charge added to a hotel bill per person or night
items.example: The city adds a tourist tax of two euros a night.

items.definitionEn: a plastic card that opens a hotel room instead of a metal key
items.example: The key card stops working if you keep it next to your phone.

items.definitionEn: a phone call from the hotel to wake you at a chosen time
items.example: Ask reception for a wake-up call at six.

items.definitionEn: a group of hotels with the same brand in many places
items.example: A hotel chain offers predictable standards, but less character.

items.definitionEn: how full a hotel is; the number of rooms in use
items.example: Summer occupancy is close to one hundred percent.

items.definitionEn: a detailed list of places, times and transport for a trip
items.example: The itinerary includes a morning in the old town and an afternoon cruise.

items.definitionEn: visiting famous buildings and places as a tourist
items.example: We spent the morning sightseeing and the afternoon in a café.

items.definitionEn: a holiday in which flights and accommodation are booked together
items.example: A package holiday is easier if you do not like planning.

items.definitionEn: a holiday price that covers meals, drinks and many activities
items.example: The all-inclusive resort includes buffet meals and soft drinks.

items.definitionEn: travelling cheaply with a rucksack, often for a long period
items.example: Backpacking around south-east Asia taught her to budget.

items.definitionEn: in places that few tourists visit
items.example: They looked for villages off the beaten track, not the resort strip.

items.definitionEn: tourism designed to protect nature and support local people
items.example: Eco-tourism in the wetlands funds bird protection.

items.definitionEn: a payment meant to balance the emissions from a journey, for example by planting trees
items.example: Some airlines let you buy a carbon offset when you book.

items.definitionEn: travel that tries not to harm the environment or local communities
items.example: Sustainable tourism limits visitor numbers in fragile areas.

items.definitionEn: when too many visitors damage a place or make life hard for residents
items.example: Overtourism has pushed up rents in the historic centre.

items.definitionEn: large numbers of people visiting the same popular places
items.example: Mass tourism filled the beach with identical hotels.

items.definitionEn: travel focused on history, art, festivals and local traditions
items.example: Cultural tourism in Kraków includes museums and folk concerts.

items.definitionEn: holidays based on physical challenge, such as trekking or rafting
items.example: Adventure tourism in the Tatras includes guided ridge walks.

items.definitionEn: holidays on working farms, often with local food and rural tasks
items.example: Agritourism let the children collect eggs and see the orchard.

items.definitionEn: a short holiday in a city, often a weekend
items.example: A city break in Lisbon is easy by train from Porto.

items.definitionEn: a visit around a place with someone who explains what you see
items.example: The guided tour of the castle lasts ninety minutes.

items.definitionEn: a short trip, often from a hotel or cruise, to see a nearby place
items.example: The hotel sells an excursion to the salt mine.

items.definitionEn: a holiday on a large ship that visits several ports
items.example: The Mediterranean cruise called at four different cities.

items.definitionEn: a company that designs and sells complete holidays
items.example: The tour operator changed the hotel two weeks before departure.

items.definitionEn: a shop that advises on and books holidays and tickets
items.example: Book the insurance at the travel agent's when you pay for the trip.

items.definitionEn: a person employed by a tour company to look after guests at a resort
items.example: The holiday rep met us in the lobby and handed out wristbands.

items.definitionEn: extra money charged when one person occupies a room meant for two
items.example: The single supplement made the trip expensive for solo travellers.

items.definitionEn: the most popular, usually most expensive, time to visit a place
items.example: Hotel prices double in peak season on the coast.

items.definitionEn: at the time of year when a destination is quiet and often cheaper
items.example: Hotels are cheaper if you travel out of season.

items.definitionEn: the busiest holiday period, when prices and crowds are at their height
items.example: Flights are scarce in high season unless you book early.

items.definitionEn: the least busy period, when prices tend to fall
items.example: Low season in Greece is milder and far quieter.

items.definitionPl: last minute, oferta na ostatnią chwilę
items.definitionEn: a cheap holiday sold shortly before departure
items.example: A last-minute deal sent us to Crete with two days' notice.

items.definitionEn: a place that charges too much because visitors do not know better
items.example: The café by the cathedral is a tourist trap with weak coffee.

items.definitionEn: a place that visitors come to see
items.example: The castle is the main tourist attraction in the valley.

items.definitionEn: a place protected because of its historical or cultural importance
items.example: The old shipyard is now a heritage site with a museum.

items.definitionEn: an excellent place that few tourists have discovered
items.example: The guidebook called the hillside chapel a hidden gem.

items.definitionEn: not damaged or made ugly by development or crowds
items.example: The western coves are still unspoilt and quiet.

items.definitionEn: attractive in a way that looks like a painting
items.example: We walked through a picturesque harbour with painted boats.

items.definitionEn: a tourist bus you can leave and rejoin at many stops with one ticket
items.example: A hop-on hop-off ticket is handy on the first day in a new city.

items.definitionEn: a recorded commentary you listen to while visiting a museum or site
items.example: The audio guide is included in the ticket price.

items.definitionEn: the money you pay to enter a museum, park or attraction
items.example: The admission fee is lower with a student card.

items.definitionEn: a ticket that lets you enter without waiting in the ordinary queue
items.example: A skip-the-line pass is worth it at the palace in August.

items.definitionEn: a person who travels cheaply with a rucksack, often staying in hostels
items.example: The hostel kitchen was full of backpacker groups cooking pasta.

items.definitionPl: wakacje połączone z pracą za granicą
items.definitionEn: a trip abroad in which you work for part of the time, often on a special visa
items.example: A working holiday in New Zealand paid for the rest of her travels.

items.definitionEn: a colourful booklet advertising holidays and destinations
items.example: The travel brochure made the resort look larger than it was.

items.definitionEn: an office that gives maps, advice and tickets to visitors
items.example: Pick up a free map at the tourist information centre.

items.definitionEn: an activity or service not included in the basic holiday price
items.example: The dolphin trip is an optional extra, not part of the package.

items.definitionEn: the weeks just before or after high season, often quieter and cheaper
items.example: May is shoulder season: warm enough to swim, but not packed.

items.definitionEn: full of visitors and souvenir shops; not very local or authentic
items.example: We left the touristy square and ate where residents eat.

items.definitionEn: with far too many people in a place
items.example: The viewpoint is overcrowded at sunset in July.

items.definitionEn: extremely impressive or beautiful
items.example: The ridge walk ends with a breathtaking view of the lake.

items.definitionEn: the historic central district of a city, often with old streets
items.example: Cafés in the old town charge more than those two streets away.

items.definitionEn: a place from which you can see a wide or famous view
items.example: The bus stops below the viewpoint; the last bit is on foot.

items.definitionEn: a path marked with signs or coloured flashes so walkers do not get lost
items.example: Follow the waymarked route to the waterfall.

items.definitionEn: real and typical of a place, not invented only for tourists
items.example: We wanted authentic street food, not a themed restaurant.

items.definitionPl: jet lag, rozstrój po zmianie strefy czasowej
items.definitionEn: tiredness and confusion after a long flight across time zones
items.example: Jet lag made it hard to stay awake at lunchtime.

items.definitionEn: bags that the airline cannot find after a flight
items.example: We reported lost luggage and were given a small overnight kit.

items.definitionEn: a policy that pays if you fall ill, cancel, or lose bags abroad
items.example: Buy travel insurance before you pay for the flights.

items.definitionEn: a situation in which a plane, train or bus leaves or arrives later than planned
items.example: There was a two-hour delay because of thunderstorms.

items.definitionEn: a flight that will not operate as planned
items.example: The cancelled flight meant we slept on the terminal floor.

items.definitionEn: when transport workers stop work, so trains, buses or planes do not run normally
items.example: A transport strike blocked the metro for a whole morning.

items.definitionEn: a passport that you cannot find while you are travelling
items.example: A lost passport means a trip to the embassy before you can fly home.

items.definitionEn: a thief who steals from bags or pockets in crowds
items.example: A pickpocket took her phone on the crowded tram.

items.definitionEn: the office of one country in another that helps its citizens and represents its government
items.example: The embassy issued an emergency travel document the next day.

items.definitionEn: a smaller official office abroad that helps travellers with documents and emergencies
items.example: The consulate can replace some papers if your wallet is stolen.

items.definitionEn: an official permission, often a stamp or document, to enter a country
items.example: You need a visa to stay longer than ninety days.

items.definitionEn: permission to pass through a country on the way to another destination
items.example: Check whether you need a transit visa for the layover in Istanbul.

items.definitionEn: a visa you apply for and receive online rather than in a passport sticker
items.example: Apply for an e-visa at least three days before you fly.

items.definitionEn: a passport with a chip storing a photograph and other identity data
items.example: A biometric passport speeds up the gates at some airports.

items.definitionEn: a form stating what goods you are bringing into a country
items.example: Fill in the customs declaration if you have gifts above the limit.

items.definitionEn: to officially take something away, for example at security or customs
items.example: Officers may confiscate unlabelled food at the border.

items.definitionEn: a formal request for an insurer to pay for a loss
items.example: File an insurance claim as soon as you have the police report.

items.definitionEn: the first amount of a loss that you pay yourself under an insurance policy
items.example: The policy has a one-hundred-pound excess on luggage claims.

items.definitionEn: money an airline may owe you after a long delay or cancellation
items.example: EU rules on flight compensation apply to many delayed departures.

items.definitionEn: sent to a different airport than the one on the ticket
items.example: The plane was diverted to Manchester because of fog in London.

items.definitionEn: unable to continue a journey, often because of cancelled transport
items.example: Hundreds of passengers were stranded when the airline collapsed.

items.definitionEn: a trick designed to take money from visitors who do not know local prices or rules
items.example: A common tourist scam is an unmetered taxi from the airport.

items.definitionEn: a private car that offers rides without official permission
items.example: Never get into an unlicensed taxi outside arrivals.

items.definitionEn: feeling ill because of the movement of a boat
items.example: Seasickness tablets helped on the choppy ferry.

items.definitionEn: feeling ill because of the movement of a plane
items.example: Airsickness is worse over turbulence if you look at a screen.

items.definitionEn: the money used in another country
items.example: Order foreign currency from the bank a week before you fly.

items.definitionEn: an office that exchanges one currency for another
items.example: The bureau de change at the station charges a high commission.

items.definitionEn: paper cheques bought in advance that can be cashed abroad
items.example: Traveller's cheques are rare now, but some guides still mention them.

items.definitionEn: a card you load with money before you travel, then spend abroad
items.example: A prepaid card can cap what you lose if it is stolen.

items.definitionEn: a plug that lets you use electrical devices in another country's sockets
items.example: Pack a travel adapter; UK plugs will not fit in France.

items.definitionEn: a label on a suitcase with your name and contact details
items.example: Put a luggage tag on the handle in case the sticker comes off.

items.definitionPl: nerka / pas na pieniądze pod ubraniem
items.definitionEn: a hidden pouch worn under clothes to keep cash and documents safe
items.example: Keep the spare card in a money belt, not in the daypack.

items.definitionEn: the document you show to get on a plane
items.example: Keep your boarding pass until you leave the arrivals hall.

items.definitionEn: an official document that identifies you and lets you travel abroad
items.example: Your passport must be valid for three months after you return.

items.definitionEn: the form and process of asking a country for permission to enter
items.example: A visa application can take several weeks in the busy season.

items.definitionEn: the documents and rules you must meet to cross into a country
items.example: Check the border requirements, including how long your passport must remain valid.

items.definitionEn: the papers you need for a trip, such as a passport, visa and tickets
items.example: Keep copies of your travel documents separate from the originals.

items.definitionEn: official government advice about safety in a country
items.example: The travel advisory warned of protests in the capital.

items.definitionEn: delays or cancellations caused by storms, snow, fog or heat
items.example: Weather disruption closed the runway until noon.

items.definitionEn: suitcases that arrive later than the passenger
items.example: The airline delivered the delayed baggage the following evening.

items.definitionEn: a bag that has been broken or torn during a journey
items.example: Photograph the damaged suitcase before you leave the carousel.

items.definitionEn: sent on a different path or via different cities than planned
items.example: We were rerouted via Vienna after the original hub closed.

items.definitionEn: a visa that allows short stays in the group of European countries that share open borders
items.example: A Schengen visa is not needed for many short tourist visits, but rules change.

items.definitionEn: a temporary travel document issued when your passport is lost or stolen
items.example: The emergency passport was valid only for the journey home.

items.definitionEn: a region of the world that uses the same clock time
items.example: New York is in a time zone five hours behind Britain in winter.

items.definitionEn: how much time is left before a passport expires
items.example: Some countries demand six months of passport validity.

items.definitionEn: suitcases put in the aircraft hold, not carried into the cabin
items.example: Liquids in hold luggage are not limited like cabin bottles.

items.definitionEn: airport security rules that limit how much liquid you may take into the cabin
items.example: Liquid restrictions still apply to bottles larger than 100 millilitres.

items.definitionEn: the right to get on the plane before other passengers
items.example: Priority boarding is sold as an extra on many cheap airlines.

items.definitionEn: not being allowed on a plane, often because it is overbooked
items.example: Denied boarding can entitle you to meals, a hotel and compensation.
